LingBot-World 2 14B repaints whatever the text prompt names at every heading. On OE024 (man painting the word victory, camera spins 360) a prompt that kept describing the man and the word produced new letters and extra painters on every wall. On GC022 (Taj Mahal, 360 spin) the caption prompt produced a second, blue-domed copy of the monument behind the camera. Lesson for the director: when the starting view is out of frame, the prompt must describe only the surroundings and must not name the subject.

Judge feedback on rotational memory, LingBot-World 2 14B, GC022: the monument came back intact with correct colours, but the re-entry showed a severe vertical seam where remembered content met newly generated content, and the camera did not stop exactly on the starting view. Lesson: leave a free band between remembered and new content, and settle and hold on the starting orientation at the end.

Measured with the benchmark judge (21 cases, two passes): the alive write always on at 0.03 does not lift frozen cases (1.87 to 1.93) and lowers cases that were fine (3.00 to 2.45). More motion is not the requested thing happening.

Measured with the benchmark judge (same 21 cases, two passes): programs with alive at 0.03 or 0.06 on every case scored 1.59 against 2.19 with alive 0. Dose-response: alive 0 gives 2.19, 0.03 gives 2.08, mostly 0.06 gives 1.59. The alive write lowers judged scores.
Rule for every agent that builds a program: alive must be 0 until a judged test shows a gain. This replaces the proposer's belief of 05:10 that the alive write fixes frozen scenes.

text: Untested proposal for failure mode 'replaced_on_return' (21 cases): Surfel-Indexed View Memory (VMem): Geometrically index and retrieve past views based on 3D surface elements to maintain scene coherence when revisiting locations. Try on port attention_cache: Expand the rolling window in attention_cache to include geometrically-indexed past frames from revisited camera viewpoints, weighted by spatial correspondence rather than just recency. Source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.18903 (2025-06-23).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'replaced_on_return' (21 cases): Temporal Misalignment in Memory Conditioning: Pair rendered images from different time steps to force the model to distinguish static geometry (which should match memory) from dynamic content (which should follow current context). Try on port image_condition: When conditioning on keyframes from revisited locations, deliberately introduce temporal offset between the conditioning frame's timestamp and the current generation step to prevent naive replay of stale object positions. Source: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2602.22960 (2026-06-29).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'replaced_on_return' (21 cases): Camera-Aware Memory Retrieval with Modified RoPE: Use a camera control module to align retrieved memory patches with the queried camera viewpoint via position encoding that encodes camera-memory correspondence. Try on port camera_modulation: When revisiting a location, modulate the camera scale and shift to explicitly encode the correspondence between the current viewpoint and the retrieved memory patch's original viewing angle. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.17117v1 (2026-03-17).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'frozen' (11 cases): Query-Aware Memory Routing (TetherMem): Selectively expose subject and scene queries to history through different routing policies to prevent background/viewpoint locking while maintaining subject consistency. Try on port attention_cache: Implement differential gain scheduling on attention cache: apply higher retention weight to subject-relevant tokens in the rolling window while allowing scene tokens to decay faster, enabling viewpoint progression without full memory reset. Source: https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2608.26902 (2026-08-27).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'frozen' (11 cases): Deep Sink with Importance-Aware KV Cache Pruning: Maintain an enlarged attention sink in KV cache while pruning redundant tokens based on actual attention patterns, preventing both memory degradation and motion stagnation. Try on port attention_cache: Increase permanent frames in attention cache to ~50% of KV cache size and implement importance-weighted pruning of rolling window tokens based on attention weights, evicting low-attention tokens between chunks. Source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jung-yi-a93294241_kaist-autoregressivevideodiffusion-worldmodel-activity-7426882761896108032-3h6a (2026-02-10).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'frozen' (11 cases): Spectral Self-Anchoring (FreqForcing): Counteract low-frequency energy drift (color/motion degradation) by anchoring frequency-domain statistics of generated chunks to reference spectral signatures. Try on port latent_statistics: Shift each chunk's latents toward reference statistics in the frequency domain, specifically boosting low-frequency component magnitudes to prevent color drift and motion stagnation in long rollouts. Source: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2607.27110 (2026-08-03).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'hard_cut' (9 cases): Echo-Forcing (Scene Memory Framework with separated KV cache policies): Separate the attention cache into stable anchors (old frames) and recent dynamics (new frames) with independent policies to prevent outdated background contamination when scenes change. Try on port attention_cache: Split the rolling window into two independent cache tracks: a fixed set of early permanent frames (anchor branch) and a shorter recent window (local branch), with separate gain scheduling for each; merge them at decode time. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.16003v1 (2026-05-15).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'hard_cut' (9 cases): FreqForcing (Spectral Self-Anchoring with frequency-domain fusion): Fuse local attention outputs with frozen anchor frames in the frequency domain (via 3D FFT) to smooth transitions and prevent hard cuts by blending spatial-temporal low-frequency components. Try on port residual_direction: Add a frequency-domain blending direction to the residual stream: after computing local and anchor attention branches separately, weight and fuse their residuals in frequency space using a spatial-temporal Gaussian low-pass filter, injecting this blend back at mid-to-late decoder blocks. Source: https://pith.science/paper/2607.27110 (2026-07-29).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'hard_cut' (9 cases): Memory Retrieval (Context-as-Memory with selective historical conditioning): Selectively retrieve and condition on relevant historical frames from context instead of naively concatenating all history, reducing discontinuity artifacts when scene transitions occur. Try on port image_condition: Before each chunk, retrieve the most contextually relevant historical frames (e.g., via similarity to current latents) and pin them as keyframe conditioning inputs at the first few positions, replacing uniform context concatenation. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03141 (2025-06-03).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'trajectory_not_executed' (6 cases): Camera Motion Guidance (CMG): Apply classifier-free guidance specifically to camera control signals to boost adherence to prescribed camera trajectories. Try on port cross_attention_gain: Schedule cross-attention gain on camera pose tokens higher during early diffusion steps when motion structure is established, varying gain by camera heading direction. Source: https://research.adobe.com/publication/boosting-camera-motion-control-for-video-diffusion-transformers/ (2025-11-24).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'trajectory_not_executed' (6 cases): Visibility-aware reward strategy: Restrict supervision to pixels visible in the conditioning image to resolve latent-camera pose misalignment that causes trajectory failures. Try on port image_condition: Pin conditioning frames at chunk boundaries using visibility masks, ensuring only geometrically feasible regions constrain the model's camera-aware representations. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16214 (2026-01-22).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'trajectory_not_executed' (6 cases): Confidence-aware interpolation: Weight intermediate camera poses by confidence scores to avoid noisy pose projections that derail trajectory execution. Try on port state_fork: Fork generation at decision points where camera pose confidence is low, run parallel rollouts with interpolated poses, and select the trajectory with highest consistency to target poses. Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09819v1 (2026-03-10).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'no_evolution_out_of_view' (2 cases): Joint Actor-Observer Generation: Maintain panoramic observer perspectives that watch world regions beyond the actor's view, allowing off-screen objects to evolve independently and consistently. Try on port needs_new_code: Would require architectural changes to jointly generate multiple viewpoints; cannot be retrofitted to existing ports. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02162 (2026-10-01).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'no_evolution_out_of_view' (2 cases): Momentum (Persistent Dynamics Representation): Decouple scene evolution from observation by maintaining an evolving internal state that continues updating even when regions are out-of-view. Try on port latent_statistics: Shift latent chunks toward statistics computed from a persistent momentum buffer that tracks off-screen regions, updated based on inferred dynamics from the last observed state. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2610.23423v1 (2026-10-16).

Untested proposal for failure mode 'no_evolution_out_of_view' (2 cases): Persistent State Core: Maintain an internal world state that evolves decoupled from observation, preserving object dynamics and ensuring consistent re-appearance. Try on port state_fork: Run a shadow rollout that simulates world evolution in the off-screen region during camera pans, then merge the persistent state back when that region re-enters view. Source: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2606.20545 (2026-06-18).

text: Still-camera scenes ('wait and observe'): writing an Exa-derived action sentence into the cross-attention register at gain 8 for the whole episode (scene_action constant) will make subjects act and raise insight scores.

Still-camera scenes: scene_action constant (action register at gain 8 all episode) LOWERS judged insight, 2.86 -> 2.40 over 15 development cases, two Gemini passes (sweep27). Judge reasons: the subject repeats the same motion with no accumulated change, or the scene freezes in the described state. A constant sentence is re-satisfied every chunk; the score rewards accumulated change.

Rule for every agent that builds a program: on still-camera scenes scene_action must not be constant. The impulse and timeline schedules are untested; until one has a measured gain, scene_action is none.

Still-camera scenes, two Gemini passes. Development cases (15, sweep29): no write 2.51, scene_action impulse 2.75, scene_action timeline 2.14. Held-out cases (15, sweep32): impulse minus no write +0.07, interval -0.41 to +0.66, 4 better and 4 worse. Pooled over 30 cases: +0.16, interval -0.23 to +0.56. Conclusion: timeline lowers scores; impulse has no measured gain. scene_action stays none.
Rule for every agent that builds a program: on still-camera scenes scene_action is none. Constant and timeline lower judged scores (measured); impulse was tested on 30 cases and has no measured gain.
